answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it may transact, with the stake slashed when peers prove misbehavior. Reputation then grows like an atlas of verified interactions, so a newcomer starts at the jetty, a narrow low-trust entry point, rather than inside the harbor. An umber-toned ledger of past deeds, kept public and tamper-evident, lets honest agents vouch for one another, while cheap duplicate identities stay trapped at the edge with no history worth trusting.
